resolutions.researcher_notes: No source names a standalone 'Khoms-Melita' pipeline as an operating asset directly, so status is inferred from context per the corridor it purports to be part of, not a literal 'operating' token. Punj Lloyd Group's own 25-years retrospective (Yumpu p.56) confirms the Tripoli-Melita segment was commissioned in March 2010 and gas has flowed from Melita to Zawia Power Plant since, replacing diesel (recurring USD 1bn/yr savings cited) -- clear evidence of an operating gas corridor through this route. OPEC's Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012 Table 4.10 ('Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011') independently lists both 'Khoms/Tripoli' and 'Tripoli/Mellitah' as live Sirte Oil-operated gas lines with length/diameter data for reporting year 2011, confirming operation as of that date. Live opec.org PDF is dead (redirects to homepage, matches the known gotcha); recovered via the 2012-07-22 Wayback snapshot and confirmed with pdftotext (url_verifier FAILs on the raw PDF bytes as expected -- manually confirmed 'Khoms/Tripoli', 'Tripoli/Mellitah', and 'Table 4.10' all present in the extracted text). IMPORTANT CAVEAT carried from the row-level validity review: no source ever names a distinct, standalone 25 km 'Khoms-Melita' object -- every source describes this corridor as the separately-tracked Khoms-Tripoli (~201km) + Tripoli-Mellitah (~158km) segments. These refs support that the Khoms-to-Mellitah gas corridor operates, not that P1789 specifically (as scoped) is a real discrete asset -- flag stands from the rows/P1789.json duplicate assessment.

Both the El Khoms-Tripoli and Tripoli-Melita lines are explicitly named 'Gas Pipeline' projects in Punj Lloyd's own retrospective (Yumpu p.55, 'El Khoms-Tripoli Gas Pipeline' / 'Tripoli-Melita Gas Pipeline'), and OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 lists them under the heading 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' (recovered via Wayback + pdftotext, live opec.org link dead per the known ASB gotcha). Two independent, well-corroborated sources for Fuel=Gas. Same corridor-vs-segment caveat as Status applies to whether this specifically supports the 25km 'Khoms-Melita' object.

Punj Lloyd's retrospective (Yumpu p.56) states the government's target for early commissioning of the Tripoli-Melita Pipeline (gas to Zawia Power Plant) was March 2010 and that Punj Lloyd achieved it, with full project completion targeted for 'first half of 2011'. Libya Herald (2020, reporting on a 2020 ICC arbitration ruling) independently corroborates the same timeline, describing the Tripoli-Khoms and Khoms-Mellitah pipeline projects as still under construction when Libya's 2011 revolution halted work. Together these two independent sources support a 2010 construction/commissioning window consistent with ConstructionYear=2010, though again describing the broader corridor rather than a distinct 25km segment.

Punj Lloyd's retrospective (Yumpu p.54) states the Tripoli-Melita Gas Pipeline distributes 'approximately 200 MMSCFD' through the new 34-inch line. 200 MMSCFD converts to ~2.07 bcm/yr (200 x 365 x 0.0283168), a close match to the stated Capacity=2.00 bcm/y (~3% off, consistent with rounding of an approximate figure). This is the only source found with a capacity figure in directly comparable units; OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 does carry a 'Capacity' column for these lines but in units (1,000 scm/yr) that appear to represent cumulative lifetime throughput rather than a nameplate annual rate (values in the tens of millions, i.e. tens of bcm, implausible as an annual rate for a single trunk line) -- did not use it as corroboration because the metric isn't clearly the same thing. Only one strong source found within session search budget (web search was rate-limited/CAPTCHA-walled partway through this shard; DDG, Bing, Ecosia, Mojeek all failed after initial queries) -- tier medium, independent=false pending a second source. Same corridor-vs-segment caveat as other units: this is the Tripoli-Melita segment's nameplate capacity, not confirmed as unique to a standalone 'Khoms-Melita' 25km object.

No source found (English or Arabic) names a distinct 25 km 'Khoms-Melita' pipeline segment. OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 (recovered via Wayback+pdftotext) explicitly lists the two real segments covering this corridor -- 'Khoms/Tripoli' at 125 miles (~201 km) and 'Tripoli/Mellitah' at 98 miles (~158 km) -- neither of which is 25 km. Punj Lloyd's retrospective corroborates similar lengths (150km+7km for El Khoms-Tripoli; a 99km branch plus the broader 1,100km Benghazi-Melita trunk for Tripoli-Melita). No source of any kind puts a 25 km figure on any Khoms-to-Mellitah/Melita gas line. This is consistent with the row-level validity finding (batches/libya-gas/staging/ref-sweep-operating/rows/P1789.json) that P1789 looks like a duplicate/mis-scoped digitization artifact rather than a real distinct 25km asset -- marking UNRESOLVED rather than force-fitting a corridor-level source that doesn't support this specific value.

OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 (Wayback+pdftotext recovery; live opec.org link is dead, known gotcha) lists both 'Khoms/Tripoli' and 'Tripoli/Mellitah' at 34-inch diameter. Punj Lloyd's retrospective (Yumpu p.54) independently confirms 34-inch pipe for both the El Khoms-Tripoli line and the new Tripoli-Melita line. Two independent sources agree exactly on 34in -- the whole Khoms-Mellitah coastal corridor appears to be uniformly 34in trunk line, so this value is well supported at the corridor level even though (per the Length note) the specific 25km 'Khoms-Melita' segment is not independently confirmed to exist as a discrete object.

Libya Herald explicitly names a 'Khoms-Mellitah pipeline project' (tying Khoms and Mellitah together as the two named endpoints), and Punj Lloyd's retrospective (Yumpu p.54) describes gas moving from the Wafa field via Tripoli 'to Melita for processing and distribution' with a compressor station at Melita -- both confirm Khoms and Melita/Mellitah as real, correctly-named endpoint locations on this coastal corridor. StartCountryOrArea/EndCountryOrArea=Libya and StartLocation=Khoms/EndLocation=Melita are supported. FLAGGING A CONTRADICTION: EndState/Province is recorded as 'Melita Port', which is not a real Libyan governorate/province -- the Mellitah Complex actually sits in Nuqat al Khams province (as GEM's own P0483/P0484 records correctly show per the row-level validity note). This province field looks like a digitization error and should be corrected/reviewed rather than referenced as-is; the ref supports the place names (Khoms, Melita/Mellitah) only, not the 'Melita Port' province value.

Three independent sources confirm Sirte Oil Co as the operator of the Khoms-Tripoli-Mellitah corridor: (1) Libya Herald -- Sirte Oil was the client/defendant in the Punj Lloyd arbitration over the Tripoli-Khoms and Khoms-Mellitah pipeline projects; (2) Punj Lloyd's own retrospective (Yumpu p.53) names 'the state-owned Sirte Oil Company Marsa El-Brega' as the contracting client for both EPC pipeline projects; (3) Sirte Oil Co's own website (Wayback snapshot of a now-dead article, sirteoil.com.ly/?p=8754, Arabic) is a tour report by Sirte Oil's own board chairman inspecting facilities including 'الخط الطولي الخمس مليته' (the Khoms-Mellitah longitudinal line), directly confirming Sirte Oil operates this named corridor. High confidence for Operator=Sirte Oil Co; OperatorLocalLanguage Arabic form (شركة سرت لإنتاج وتصنيع النفط والغاز) matches the company referenced in source (3), which uses the shorter 'شركة سرت للنفط' / trading name.

No primary NOC (noclibya.com.ly) or Sirte Oil (sirteoil.com.ly) company-profile page could be recovered (current noclibya.com.ly site has no subsidiaries page; older Wayback snapshots of both domains checked and none surfaced an explicit ownership statement). Best available support: Wikipedia's Sirte Oil Company article states plainly 'Sirte Oil Company (SOC) ... is an oil and gas company in Libya operating under the state-owned National Oil Corporation (NOC)' and that it 'was formed as a NOC subsidiary' in 1981 -- directly supports Owner1=Libyan National Oil Corp, Owner1%=100%. Corroborated (weakly, not independently on the ownership fact itself) by Punj Lloyd's retrospective (Yumpu p.53) describing Sirte Oil as 'the state-owned Sirte Oil Company'. Tier medium (Wikipedia is a single, tertiary-but-verifiable source for the specific NOC-subsidiary claim; not GEM/blocklisted). Flagging for review: this establishes Sirte Oil Co -> NOC ownership generally, not specific to a confirmed standalone 'Khoms-Melita' pipeline asset (see Length note re: existence concern).
